scope: SwitchControl tweak safety audit — registry + network tweaks

changes.whoShouldAvoidAdded: Anyone who prints, even occasionally. Students, offices, remote workers, and anyone with network or wireless printers.
changes.rationale: Disabling Print Spooler removes ALL printing capability (local and network). It is a known security surface but this is not a reasonable tradeoff for general users. Reclassified as Risky.

changes.whoShouldAvoidAdded: Anyone using Bluetooth headsets, wireless controllers, Bluetooth mice/keyboard, or Bluetooth speakers.
changes.rationale: Disabling Bluetooth breaks ALL Bluetooth devices including controllers, headsets, mice, and keyboards. This was incorrectly marked Safe/Recommended. AudioGuard now blocks this from bulk apply when audio devices are detected.

changes.whoShouldAvoidAdded: Laptop users, anyone relying on Wi-Fi as primary or backup connection, users without a working Ethernet connection.
changes.rationale: Wi-Fi disable removes ALL Wi-Fi connectivity. On laptops or systems without Ethernet, this causes total internet loss. Upgraded from Moderate to Risky with explicit connectivity pre-check warning.

changes.whoShouldAvoidAdded: Developers using WSL2, Docker Desktop, or Windows Sandbox. Anyone using Android apps on Windows.
changes.rationale: Hyper-V disable breaks WSL2, Docker Desktop, Windows Sandbox, and Android Subsystem. Many developers and power users rely on these. Upgraded from Moderate to Risky with expanded whoShouldAvoid.

changes.whoShouldAvoidAdded: Users with HDD boot drives. On SSD/NVMe systems the risk is low.
changes.rationale: Disabling Prefetch noticeably slows cold-boot app launches on HDDs. Modern systems already handle caching through SysMain/Superfetch. Upgraded from Safe to Moderate with HDD-specific warning.

changes.whoShouldAvoidAdded: Users with many open Explorer windows who would lose their current folder positions on restart.
changes.rationale: Requires Windows Explorer restart — all open file windows close. This can be disruptive to users with many active Explorer sessions. Downgraded from Recommended/Advanced to Moderate.

changes.warningAdded: Affects all TCP traffic system-wide. Monitor ping after applying. May not improve UDP-based games.
changes.rationale: Global TCP change that affects all traffic, not just games. UDP-based games see no benefit. Can increase TCP overhead and jitter on some connections. NetworkGuard now monitors ping before/after.

changes.warningAdded: CTCP can increase jitter on lossy links. Default Cubic is optimal for most gaming. Monitor ping carefully.
changes.rationale: CTCP is more aggressive than Cubic (default) and can actually worsen latency on lossy or rate-limited links. Default Cubic is optimal for most gaming. Upgraded to Risky/Experimental.

changes.warningAdded: Forces CPU to handle network work. Can reduce throughput and increase latency on modern NICs. Not recommended for gaming.
changes.rationale: Forces CPU to handle work normally offloaded to the NIC, significantly increasing CPU load. Can reduce throughput and increase latency on modern NICs. Not recommended for gaming. Upgraded to Risky/Experimental.

changes.unavailableReason: TCP autotuning is already enabled by default in Windows 10/11. Manually setting it provides no benefit and is not recommended for gaming optimization.
changes.rationale: This tweak has no practical effect — autotuning is already on by default. Marked unavailable to prevent users from thinking it does something useful.

changes.warningAdded: Disabling UDP offloads increases CPU load. Verify with ping/latency testing before and after applying.
changes.rationale: Forces CPU to handle UDP checksums. Can increase CPU usage and reduce throughput on high-bandwidth UDP streams. Added explicit CPU warning.

changes.warningAdded: Usually already disabled in modern Windows. Verify before applying.
changes.rationale: Modern Windows already has heuristics disabled by default. Added warning to prevent unnecessary application.

AudioGuard.behavior: Blocks bulk apply when active Bluetooth/audio devices detected. Allows individual apply with warning.

NetworkGuard.behavior: Captures baseline gateway ping before apply. Post-check after apply. Auto-rollback if ping increases by >20ms or >25%.
